title: Second class widened: all Spirit-opposed fleshly acts until repentance
source_text: XXXI. In hac classe ponenda sunt, non modo illa quae nominatim enumerantur ab Apostolo, sed caetera omnia sive externa, sive interna quae sunt ejusdem rationis, ut aperte indicavit Apostolus in hoc loco posteriore, in quo dixit, quod qui faciunt haec & similia, excludentur e regno Dei. Similia autem habentur omnia in quibus carni concupiscenti adversus Spiritum praestatur obedientia, usque ad perpetrationem actionis impiae. Haec enim omnia mortalia usitate dicuntur, quia statuunt peccantem sub novo reatu mortis, & in via ad infernum, donec per resipiscentiam ab hujusmodi peccatis desistat: juxta dictum Apostoli Rom. 8. Si secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini; si autem spiritu facta carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis.
pass_a_gloss: In this class are to be placed not only those which are named by the Apostle, but all other things whether external or internal which are of the same reason, as the Apostle openly indicated in this latter place when he said that they who do these and like things shall be excluded from the kingdom of God. And like things are held to be all those in which obedience is rendered to the flesh lusting against the Spirit, even unto the perpetration of an impious action. For all these are commonly called mortal, because they set the sinner under a new guilt of death, and on the way to hell, until by repentance he desists from such sins: according to the Apostle’s saying in Romans 8, If you live according to the flesh, you shall die; but if by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live.
pass_b_english: The second mortal class covers every flesh-obedient act—outer or inner—until repentance quits the hellward road.
